title: Trump Disclosed 1,156 July Trades, Including $25 Million Microsoft and Amazon Sales
excerpt: The 37-page filing shows $79 million to $270 million in transactions — and a quick round-trip in two Big Tech names.
body:
• President Donald Trump's latest financial disclosure lists 1,156 July securities transactions totaling between $79 million and $270 million, per a CNBC analysis.
  • The largest moves were July 20 sales of $5 million to $25 million each in Microsoft and Amazon, plus large Oracle sales.
  • Three days later the filing shows smaller repurchases of both stocks; the White House says independent managers make all investment decisions.

President Donald Trump disclosed more than 1,100 securities transactions made on his behalf in July, including sales of as much as $25 million each of Microsoft and Amazon shares, as his investment portfolio went through another month of heavy trading. The 37-page filing lists 1,156 purchases and sales totaling between roughly $79 million and $270 million, according to a CNBC analysis. Purchases totaled at least $43.6 million; sales totaled at least $35.6 million — a broad reshuffling rather than a concentrated bet.

The biggest trades

The largest transactions came on July 20: sales of between $5 million and $25 million each in Microsoft and Amazon, alongside sales of $1 million to $5 million of Oracle and a $250,001-to-$500,000 sale of Northrop Grumman. The Northrop sale landed the same day Trump signed an executive order tightening supply-chain requirements for defense contractors and restricting waivers for certain critical materials sourced from China — though the disclosure does not show what time the trade occurred or who made the investment decision.

Three days later, the filing shows repurchases: $100,001 to $250,000 of Microsoft and $1,001 to $15,000 of Amazon. July 20 was also a blockbuster session for technology stocks broadly, which added $291 billion in market value in a single day.

Where the money went

On the buy side, the filing lists $1 million-to-$5 million purchases of Intuit and Marvell Technology, $500,001-to-$1 million purchases of Nvidia, CrowdStrike, Datadog and Palo Alto Networks, and a $1 million-to-$5 million purchase of an iShares Russell 1000 ETF. The pattern — selling mega-cap names into strength while adding cybersecurity and chip stocks — reads as active sector rotation inside a large-cap technology portfolio.

"All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers. There are no conflicts of interest."

— Davis Ingle, White House spokesman

The performance question

The sales carry an awkward postscript. Since July 20, Microsoft shares have gained 24 percent, rising from $402.29 to $498.66, while Amazon added 2.1 percent, from $249.99 to $255.20, according to market data compiled this week. The sales themselves were far too small to move either stock — even the maximum $25 million figure is a fraction of a basis point of either company's market value. Fortune noted the sheer volume makes for an unusual presidential portfolio, reporting that Trump has traded more stocks than all of Congress combined.

Why it matters

For investors, the filing is a reminder that presidential portfolios have become actively traded vehicles with legible sector views — the July rotation favored cybersecurity and semiconductors over mega-cap software. Indian investors watching from abroad hold many of the same names through mutual funds and US-stock platforms; the disclosure bands are wide, but the direction of the rotation is clear. The White House maintains the accounts are discretionary and managed by third-party institutions without Trump's input.

What's next

The disclosure covers July only; August and September filings will show whether the rotation continued. Ethics watchdogs will keep pressing on timing — particularly trades adjacent to executive actions affecting the same industries.
